newsitem.title: USA: MGM Grand to spend $700 million on Las Vegas resort.
newsitem.headline: MGM Grand to spend $700 million on Las Vegas resort.

text.p: MGM Grand Inc. said Tuesday it will spend $700 million to redesign its MGM Grand Hotel/Casino resort in Las Vegas, triple the amount it previously had planned.

The company said in a statement that "significant additions and enhancements" at the 114-acre casino, which it will relaunch as "The City of Entertainment," will include expansion of the resort's casino capacity by nearly 20 percent to more than 200,000 square feet. MGM had previously announced a $250 million master plan to redesign the resort.
The new plans also call for a new 1,500-room Marriott Marquis hotel, a "mansion" with 30 suites and villas; a conference centre and a 6.6-acre pool and spa complex, the company said.

Keeping guard over everything will be a new 45-foot polished bronze lion sculpture, the resort's signature, adjoining a re-themed entertainment casino that will include a Rainforest Cafe and a nightclub, MGM Grand said.
The company also announced that by the year 2000 it will begin construction of a 500-room Ritz-Carlton Hotel at MGM Grand Las Vegas.

It said MGM Grand, Marriott International Inc. and The Ritz-Carlton Hotel Co. L.L.C. agreed in principle, subject to the negotiation of definitive agreements, to develop the Marriott Marquis and Ritz-Carlton hotels.
MGM Grand will be the owner of the hotels with Marriott and Ritz-Carlton serving as the management operators.
MGM Grand Chief Operating Officer Alex Yemenidjian said the resort, except for the Ritz-Carlton, will be completed by late 1999.
He said about $500 million of the investment will be financed from the company's free cash flow and the remainder from the company's $1 billion credit line.
